title: Studio flow status must render "disabled by deployment policy" distinctly from a binding failure (follows objectstack#17396 ruling G)
body:
Follows objectstack-ai/objectstack#17396's ruling G (2026-09-12): time-triggered flows (`schedule`, `timeRelative`) are gated by a deployment-level switch whose global default is OFF. When off, the automation engine will report every such flow as not bound with a DISTINCT reason — disabled by deployment policy — separate from a binding failure.

Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectstack#17396

## What Studio has to show

`packages/app-shell/src/views/setup/packagedFlows.ts` reads the engine's flow runtime states (`bound: false` today reads as a problem). Once the platform carries the policy reason, the flow status must render it as **"scheduled flows are disabled on this deployment"** (with the variable's name, so an operator knows where to switch it on), ⛔ not as an error and ⛔ not as "binding failed". A flow that is unbound for any other reason keeps today's rendering.

## Why it is filed now

The ruling's consequence 3 names this surface. Without a distinct rendering, every private deployment that has not switched scheduled flows on will show its packaged time-triggered flows as broken and file bugs against them; the whole point of the platform's reason code is that the console can tell the two apart.

## Acceptance

1. With the platform reporting the policy reason, the Setup flows view shows the policy sentence and no error styling for those flows.
2. A flow unbound for a real binding failure still shows the failure.
3. The exact reason-code shape is the platform's (objectstack#17396's implementation); this card follows it and does not invent one — if the platform ships a string, render the string.
